topic: The cost of a 1% investment fee
hook: One percent sounds tiny, but this fee could cost you almost two hundred thousand dollars.

blocks.narration: One percent sounds tiny, but this fee could cost you almost two hundred thousand dollars. Most people never even notice it.
blocks.visual: Close-up of a tiny clay ant carrying away a gold coin from a large pile, the pile already noticeably smaller

blocks.narration: Imagine one hundred thousand dollars invested for thirty years, earning seven percent a year before any fees are taken out.
blocks.visual: A neat stack of gold coins on a pedestal with a clay calendar beside it showing thirty pages

blocks.narration: With no fees, it grows to about seven hundred sixty-one thousand dollars. That is the power of compounding working fully for you.
blocks.visual: The coin stack grows into a tall glowing tower, camera tilting up to follow it

blocks.narration: Now take one percent off every single year. The same money ends near five hundred seventy-four thousand dollars instead.
blocks.visual: A second tower grows beside the first but stops far lower, a gap of empty space between them

blocks.narration: That gap is roughly one hundred eighty-seven thousand dollars, paid out quietly, a little every year, whether the fund wins or loses.
blocks.visual: The empty space between the towers fills with ghostly transparent coins drifting away

blocks.narration: Fees compound just like returns, except they compound against you. The dollars you lose early would have grown for decades.
blocks.visual: A small snowball rolls downhill, growing into a giant boulder made of coins

blocks.narration: Look for the expense ratio on any fund you own. Broad index funds often charge a small fraction of one percent.
blocks.visual: A magnifying glass hovers over a fund fact sheet, focusing on a small highlighted box

blocks.narration: Costs are one thing in investing you fully control. Check your expense ratio today, and send this to a friend who never has.
blocks.visual: The full tall coin tower glows warmly as the camera slowly pulls back

cta: Check your fund's expense ratio today, and send this to the friend who never has.

captions.hook_line: That tiny 1% fee could quietly eat almost $187,000 of your money 😬
captions.body: On $100,000 growing 30 years, a 7% return ends near $761k. Lose 1% a year to fees and it ends near $574k. Fees are charged every year, on everything, whether the fund wins or loses.
